issues.description: The template declares the program entry symbol as 'start' (global start / start:) while the solution uses 'main' (global main / main:). The problem statement instructs students only to change the register typo (ecc -> ecx) and does not mention any entry-point naming. This mismatch can confuse students about what the correct entry label should be and may cause linking/runtime differences depending on the build setup (Makefile/crt expectations).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the entry-point naming consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the template to use 'global main' and 'main:' to match the solution, or (B) update the solution and (optionally) the problem statement so that both use 'start'. Also clarify in the problem statement which entry label students should keep, so students only need to fix the intended register typo (ecc -> ecx) without being uncertain about the expected label name.

issues.description: The template defines the program entry label as 'start' (global start / start:) while the solution uses 'main' (global main / main:). The problem statement does not reference the entry-label name, so this cross-artifact difference is likely an unintended naming mismatch that can confuse students when they compare template and solution (they may wonder whether they must rename the entry point in addition to the instructed register fix).
issues.suggested_fix: Use the same entry-point identifier in both artifacts. Prefer changing the template to match the solution: replace 'global start' with 'global main' and rename the label 'start:' to 'main:'. This keeps the template aligned with the solution and removes unnecessary student confusion.
